text: Security is a key part of web development. First, websites should use HTTPS to encrypt data between the user and the server. This protects passwords and personal information from attackers. Second, authentication helps confirm that users are who they claim to be. Strong passwords and two-factor authentication make accounts safer. Third, input validation checks the data users enter, preventing harmful code from reaching the system. Developers must also learn about common vulnerabilities, such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting, which can damage a website or steal data. By following these practices, developers can build safer and more trustworthy applications.
